sources.entry: Hypersomnia - Competitive top-down shooter blending Counter-Strike with Hotline Miami. Runs on Linux, Windows, MacOS and the Web. (Demo) AGPL-3.0 C++/Docker

summary.one_liner: Hypersomnia is an open-source, multiplayer top-down shooter written in C++ without a game engine, with a built-in map editor and embedded server.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes a competitive top-down shooter that combines Counter-Strike-style tactics with Hotline Miami-style dynamics, featuring 24 firearms, 10 community maps, and Bomb defusal and Gun game modes. The game and its server, masterserver, and map editor are all in one executable, so players can host a server from the main menu with automatic port forwarding. The editor is built with ImGui and works directly on the game world, supports custom PNG/WAV/OGG resources and GIFs, and lets you playtest a work-in-progress map with one click. Maps are defined in a JSON format. Networking uses cross-platform deterministic simulation, so only player inputs are sent over the network, and browser and native clients can play on the same servers. The README also describes a self-updater that verifies signatures against a hardcoded developer key, and Discord and Telegram notifications for server events.
use_cases: play a multiplayer shooter with friends
host a private game server for a community
playtest and build custom shooter maps
play competitive 1v1 or team shooter matches in the browser
study deterministic networking in a C++ game
how_to_run: Play in the browser from the project's website (the README links to a browser version)
Download a native build for Windows, Linux, or macOS from the README's download section, or via Steam
Host a server using the in-game Interactive Server Setup, or use the Docker or AppImage options linked in the README
To build from source, follow BUILDING.md as referenced in the README
notable: Cross-platform deterministic simulation: only player inputs are networked, and browser and native clients (including ARM) stay in sync
Game, editor, and masterserver are all embedded in one executable, so the editor can start a playtest server and return to the editor unchanged
Browser and native clients can play on the same servers via libdatachannel and datachannel-wasm
Pool allocator with deterministic IDs and undo support for editor commands
Self-updater that checks update signatures against a hardcoded developer key
caveats: The README says the project is in very active development and may change significantly without notice
Documentation is described as a WIP wiki; the game guide and build instructions are in separate files (GUIDE.md, BUILDING.md)
Ranked play and Discord/Steam account linking are features of the official online service described in the README
